motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Iitah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Fiscal Year 2019-202A Budget ¿nd Certified 'fax Rate" Mr. Jerome presented the fiscal year 2019-2020 budget and gave an overview of the budgeted expenses and revenues. He stated the projected revenues are $107,142 more than the projected expenditures; this balance will go towards the Fund Balance Reserve. Mr. Jerome explained the following changes made to the budget since it was presented to the Council on May 21,2019. The General Fund revenue was decreased by $59,000. This is due to vehicles being fully depreciated in the funds to which the vehicles are assigned" Since the vehicles are purchased on a State contract, the City obtains them at a reduced price. The additional gain the City receives at the sale of the vehicles will be recognized in the assigned fund. The General Fund expenditures have been increased by $141,636. The increases include $35,000 for a vehicle for a new employee in the Engineering Department, the use of $60,000 of the Fund Balance for General Fund capital projects, $40,000 for phase two of the Utah State University water conservation project, and $18,500 for records management software. This software was budgeted in the current fiscal year budget and has been moved to the fiscal year 2019-2020 budget. The Finance Department has had a change in staff which reduced expenditures by $11,864. The Enterprise Fund change is due to the gain the City will see in vehicle sales. The Capital Projects Fund includes the completion of all of the projects on the Council's priority list. The addition of $60,000 from the Fund Balance allows all projects to be budgeted for fiscal year 2019-2020. Mr. Jerome explained Utah County adjusts the certified tax rate based on the value of improvements in the City. If home values increaseo the tax rate goes downo and vice versa; this allows taxes paid to remain the same year over year. This protection was put in place to allow municipalities to maintain existing levels of service" The rate this year will be 0.000825 percent. The rate has continued to fall since 2012, which is due to values increasing. I9. RESOLTJT'ION/EAGT,EHEIGFITSVII,I,AGE 19.4. Economic Development Director Aaron Sanborn explained the ladder signs in the City were previously managed by the Lehi Area Chamber of Commerce. The program is now being administered by the City until the Eagle Mountain City Chamber of Commerce begins management. He said the current Municipal Code is sparse in details regarding program administration. This updated Code will set a priority list for entities advertising on the ladder signs, giving priority to local commercial and home-based businesses. It also adds language to create an application process. Approved maps specify locations where signs can be added. The sign locations are at least 1,000 feet apart, except in specific locations with high traffic and commercial uses. Signs that pose traffic hazards will be moved. New signs will only be added when all existing sign space is in use. Mr. Sanborn said items for the Council to consider include a potential limitation to the number of signs an entity can lease, a process in which an entity can use to install a sign in a location not on the approved sign location maps, and where the applications will be submitted. Applications can be submitted to the Economic Development Director, or to the Eagle Mountain Chamber of Commerce, if an agreement is in place
